Campbell Jr.]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[David Beasley]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsSC}} The '''1994 South Carolina gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994, to select the [[Governor of South Carolina|governor]] of the state of [[South Carolina]]. The contest featured two politicians from [[the Upstate]] and [[David Beasley]] narrowly defeated [[Nick Theodore]] to become the [[List of governors of South Carolina|113th governor]] of South Carolina. ==Democratic primary== The [[South Carolina Democratic Party]] held their [[Partisan primary|primary]] for governor on August 9, 1994. [[Lieutenant Governor of South Carolina|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Nick Theodore]], from [[the Upstate]], emerged as the winner of the runoff election on August 23 against popular [[Charleston, South Carolina|Charleston]] mayor [[Joseph P. Riley Jr.|Joseph P. (Joe) Riley Jr.]] and the three-term [[Attorney General of South Carolina]], [[Thomas T. Medlock]]. === Candidates === * William Holler * [[Thomas T. Beasley cruised to victory and benefited from the campaign of popular [[Charleston, South Carolina|Charleston]] mayor [[Joseph P. Riley Jr.|Joe Riley]] for the Democratic nomination by drawing Lowcountry voters away from the Republican primary and towards the Democratic primary. ===Candidates=== * [[David Beasley]], state representative from [[Society Hill, South Carolina|Society Hill]] * [[Thomas Hartnett]], former U.S. representative from Charleston * [[Arthur Ravenel Jr.]], U.S. representative from Charleston === Results === {{Election box begin no change|title=1994 Republican gubernatorial primary}} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = [[David Beasley]] |party = Republican Party (US) |votes = 119,724 |percentage = 47.19% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = [[Arthur Ravenel Jr.]] |party = Republican Party (US) |votes = 81,129 |percentage = 31.98% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |candidate = [[Thomas Hartnett]] |party = Republican Party (US) |votes = 52,866 |percentage = 20.84% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 253,719 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} === Runoff results === {{Election box begin |title=1994 Republican gubernatorial runoff}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link |candidate = [[David Beasley]] |party = Republican Party (US) |votes = 134,297 |percentage = 57.59% | change = {{increase}}10.40 }} {{Election box candidate with party link |candidate = [[Arthur Ravenel Jr.]] |party = Republican Party (US) |votes = 98,915 |percentage = 42.41% | change = {{increase}}10.43 }} {{Election box total | votes = 233,212 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" !
